scheme_name: AGR-61 Agro Service Providers for the Purpose of Making Farming More Profitable With the Help of Farm Mechanization
description:
The AGR-61 Agro Service Providers scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This initiative aims to enhance the profitability of farming through the adoption of farm mechanization. 

The scheme is part of the broader strategy to modernize agriculture in India. 

The Indian agricultural sector has been facing challenges such as low productivity and labor shortages. 

To address these issues, the AGR-61 scheme focuses on providing farmers with access to modern agricultural machinery. 

The primary objective of the AGR-61 scheme is to increase the efficiency of agricultural operations. 

The scheme aims to reduce the cost of production for farmers by promoting the use of mechanized farming techniques. 

The government has set a target to increase the adoption of farm mechanization by 30% by the year 2025. 

The scheme also aims to improve the income of farmers by at least 20% through enhanced productivity. 

Under this scheme, various types of agricultural machinery are made available to farmers. 

These include tractors, harvesters, seeders, and other essential equipment. 

The government provides subsidies to eligible farmers for the purchase of these machines. 

The subsidy amount can be as high as 50% of the total cost of the machinery. 

For small and marginal farmers, the subsidy can go up to 80% in certain cases. 

This financial assistance significantly reduces the burden on farmers. 

Farmers can avail of these subsidies through registered Agro Service Providers. 

These providers are trained and certified by the government to ensure quality service delivery. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers to benefit from the AGR-61 scheme include being a resident of India. 

Farmers must also possess a valid land ownership document. 

The landholding should not exceed 5 hectares for small and marginal farmers. 

Farmers must be engaged in agricultural activities and have a minimum annual income of INR 1 lakh. 

The application process for the AGR-61 scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers need to visit the nearest Agro Service Provider office. 

They must fill out an application form and submit it along with required documents. 

Documents required include proof of identity, land ownership documents, and income certificates. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the Agro Service Provider. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 days. 

Upon successful verification, farmers will receive a confirmation of their eligibility. 

The subsidy amount will then be processed for disbursement. 

Disbursement of the subsidy is usually completed within 30 days of approval. 

Farmers can also track the status of their application online through the official government portal. 

The AGR-61 scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The Department of Agriculture and Cooperation is the primary agency overseeing the scheme. 

Farmers can contact the Ministry at their official helpline number 1800 180 1551 for assistance. 

The scheme is expected to benefit over 1 million farmers across the country. 

It is particularly focused on regions with high agricultural potential. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the initial phase of the scheme. 

This budget will be utilized for subsidies and training programs for Agro Service Providers. 

Training programs are designed to enhance the skills of service providers in operating and maintaining machinery. 

The government also plans to conduct awareness campaigns to educate farmers about the benefits of mechanization. 

These campaigns will be held in collaboration with local agricultural universities and institutions. 

The AGR-61 scheme is aligned with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The initiative also supports the Atmanirbhar Bharat mission by promoting self-reliance in agriculture. 

Farm mechanization is expected to lead to a significant reduction in labor costs. 

It will also help in timely operations such as sowing and harvesting. 

The use of modern machinery is projected to increase crop yields by up to 25%. 

Farmers using mechanized methods can save up to 40% on input costs. 

The scheme encourages the formation of farmer producer organizations. 

These organizations can collectively purchase machinery, reducing individual costs. 

The government is also exploring partnerships with private sector companies for better technology transfer. 

This collaboration aims to bring cutting-edge agricultural technology to Indian farmers. 

The AGR-61 scheme is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at sustainable agriculture. 

It complements other schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi and Soil Health Card Scheme. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of mechanization reach the most vulnerable farmers. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted to assess its impact. 

Feedback from farmers will be collected to make necessary adjustments to the scheme. 

The success of the AGR-61 scheme will be measured by the increase in farm productivity and income levels. 

Overall, the AGR-61 Agro Service Providers scheme represents a significant step towards modernizing Indian agriculture. 

It aims to empower farmers with the tools they need to succeed in a competitive market. 

The scheme is expected to transform the agricultural landscape of India in the coming years. 

By promoting mechanization, the government hopes to create a more resilient agricultural sector. 

This initiative is crucial for ensuring food security and improving the livelihoods of millions of farmers. 

The AGR-61 scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to enhancing the agricultural economy of India.
